title: A colony that breeds, and one that cannot — same world, same moment
question: One of these has 186 ant cells in frame and the other 66. Can you see any difference at all?
context_md:
Pricing the routes that would let an ant afford a child (Lane I). One combination works: the colony in one of these panes **bred 79 times and grew from 38 ants to 106**; the other never managed a single birth and is the ant that ships today. Same world seed, same frame, same crop.

**I cannot find the ants in either picture, and that is why I am asking rather than telling.** The counts under each pane are measured inside the rendered window, so they are in shot — 186 of them in one case. If the two read the same to you, then the whole reproduction economy is invisible to a player whichever route gets built, and that is a bigger finding than which route wins.

What I am *not* asking about: the trees and the ground differ slightly because the two runs diverge after the first birth. Ignore that — the question is only whether a colony three times the size looks like one.
